To determine the number of possible values of \( S \), the sum of a 90-element subset \(\mathcal{A}\) of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, 100\}\), we consider the complement subset. The sum \( S \) can be expressed as \( 5050 - \text{(sum of the excluded 10 elements)} \), where 5050 is the total sum of the numbers from 1 to 100.

First, we calculate the minimum and maximum possible sums of the excluded 10-element subsets:
